page: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 768 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. For local persistence and high-speed caching, the instance bundles 22,500 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 56 Gbps. The platform does not include discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong parallel processing and cryptographic performance. In PassMark testing, the CPU encryption evaluation scored 87,228.27, reaching top-decile performance due to hardware-assisted AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Multi-core performance is robust, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 92,861.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,841.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 322.22 GB/s, while write bandwidth registered 139.48 GB/s. Transactional efficiency is demonstrated by 89.14 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. However, single-core benchmarks remain moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,642.0, and large-scale language model inference throughput declines sharply on larger parameter architectures due to the lack of dedicated accelerators.

By coupling 22.5 TB of local NVMe storage with extensive memory and high networking bandwidth, the instance provides dense local capacity without relying on external network-attached volumes. This architecture suits distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational databases, large-scale search indices, in-memory caching systems, and real-time analytical processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, it is configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores using an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz, 768 GB of DDR4 memory, and 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network capacity offers a 56 Gbps baseline. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier cryptographic execution alongside strong multi-core processing, sustained memory bandwidth, and high-frequency in-memory database transactions, yielding 89.14 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core benchmarks reflect moderate throughput, and LLM text generation is constrained by the absence of discrete GPU accelerators. The instance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding high IOPS and large local storage, making it suitable for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, large-scale search engines, and real-time analytical processing.
